settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal bandit on no-backdoor graphs (simple regret)
unmapped: 2M+1 arms: do(X_i=x) for M binary intervenable nodes plus the observational arm do()
no backdoor paths from intervenable nodes to reward Y, so E[Y|do(X_i=x)] = E[Y|X_i=x]
observational arm reveals sampled X_i values (causal side information)
interventions cost gamma >= 1, observation costs 1; total budget B known to learner
p = min_{i,x} P(X_i=x) > 0, unknown to learner
settings.definition_quote: we assume that there are no backdoor paths from $X_i$ to the reward variable. This implies $E[Y \mid do(X_i=x)] = E[Y\mid X_i=x] = \mu_{i,x}$ ... an algorithm for this problem is given as input the graph $\mathcal{G}$, the set of intervenable nodes $\{X_1, \ldots, X_M\}$, a budget $B$, and $\gamma$ which is the cost for pulling an arm $a_{i,x}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal bandit on no-backdoor graphs (cumulative regret)
unmapped: no-backdoor causal graph with 2M+1 arms incl. observational arm giving side information
intervention cost gamma, observation cost 1, budget B; regret defined as G_B - G_ALG(B) relative to the best budgeted policy
settings.definition_quote: Let $G_\mathtt{ALG}(B)$ be the expected reward accumulated by algorithm $\mathtt{ALG}$ with budget $B$, and let $G_B = \max_{\mathtt{ALG}} G_\mathtt{ALG}(B)$. Then, the cumulative regret ... $R_{\mathtt{ALG}}(B) = G_B - G_\mathtt{ALG}(B)$

settings.name_in_paper: Non-budgeted causal bandit on general graphs with known parent distributions
unmapped: learner is given P(Pa(Y)=y | do(a)) for all interventions a
parent distributions under all interventions share the same non-zero support
reward parents Pa(Y) observed each round; n parents each taking k values
settings.definition_quote: We assume the following: (a) the algorithm receives as input $\mathbb{P}(Pa(Y)= \mathbf{y}| do(a))$ for all $a$, and (b) the distributions $\mathbb{P}(Pa(Y)= \mathbf{y}| do(a))$ for all $a$ have the same non-zero support.

source.label: theorem: simple regret observational algorithm
source.quote: The expected simple regret of \OBSALG with budget $B$ is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{pB}\log (pMB)}\right)$.

results.notes: Proof uses B >= L (a constant depending on p, M).

conditions: B sufficiently large (B >= max(gamma m, pM) and B >= (16/p^2) log terms)

source.label: theorem: simple regret of gammapba
source.quote: If $\gamma \geq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then the expected simple regret of \GammaPBA is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{pB}\log (pMB)}\right)$, and if $\gamma \leq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then it is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}{B}\log \frac{MB}{\gamma \cdot m(\mathbf{p})}}\right)$.

source.label: theorem: simple regret of gammapba
source.quote: if $\gamma \leq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then it is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}{B}\log \frac{MB}{\gamma \cdot m(\mathbf{p})}}\right)$.

conditions: observational arm is optimal in cost-weighted sense (a^* = a_0)

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret of gamma paralllel bandit
source.quote: If $a^* = a_0$ then the expected cumulative regret of the algorithm is $O(1)$ and otherwise ...

results.notes: Proof gives 1 + 2M pi^2 (gamma-1)/3 + sum Delta_a pi^2/3. Regret is relative to best budgeted policy G_B; algorithm is budget-oblivious, so marked anytime.

symbols.Delta_i: Delta_{i,x} = mu_{a*} - mu_{i,x}, sum over interventional arms with positive Delta
symbols.d_i: d_{i,x} = v_{a*} - v_{i,x} with v_{i,x} = mu_{i,x}/gamma

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret of gamma paralllel bandit
source.quote: otherwise the expected cumulative regret of the algorithm is of order $\sum_{\Delta_{i,x}>0} \Delta_{i,x}\left(\text{max}\left(0, 1+ 8\ln B\left(\frac{1}{d_{i,x}^2} - \frac{p_{i,x}}{3d_0^2}\right) \right) + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\right) + \Delta_0 \left(\frac{50\ln B}{d_{0}^2} + 1 + \frac{\pi^2}{3} \right)$.

results.notes: Proof's final expression has p_{i,x}/(9 d_0^2) instead of /(3 d_0^2) and slightly different constants; recorded theorem statement. Sum is over (i,x) pairs.

symbols.L_a: max{L_1, L_{2,a}}, L_1 = min{t : t >= 2 log(k^n t^2)/delta_c^2}, L_{2,a} = min{t : t >= 4 log(k^n t^2/2) zeta_a^2 / Delta_a^2}

conditions: all parent distributions have the same non-zero support
unique optimal arm (assumed WLOG in proof)

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret for general graphs
source.quote: Let $\delta = \min_{\mathbf{y}\in S^n} \{c_{\mathbf{y}} > 0\}$, $L_1 = ...$, $L_a = \text{max}\{L_1,L_{2,a}\}$. Then the expected cumulative regret of \CUCBTwo after $T$ rounds is at most $ \sum_{a\in \mathcal{A}} \Delta_a \Big(L_a + \frac{2\pi^2}{3}\Big).$
